title.en: Estimated planetary Kp is 1.67 (quiet) at 08:00 UTC on 20 September 2026.
title.zh: 2026 年 9 月 20 日 08:00 UTC，估計行星 Kp 為 1.67（平靜）。

summary.en: Latest hour-start estimated Kp = 1.67 (label 2M). Last-180-sample maximum is 3.00 (still present in the 05:00 UTC hour; last-180 window begins about 05:19 UTC); published-window maximum is 3.00 (first at 04:30 UTC on 20 September). Hours through 01:00 UTC have rolled out of the public window; 02:00 UTC is partially rolled out (39 samples from 02:21). Completed bins 03:00–07:00 UTC closed at 0.67 / 3.00 / 3.00 / 1.33 / 1.67 respectively (03:00 peak 1.00 / 1Z at 03:42, closed at 0.67 / 1M, 60 samples; 04:00 peak 3.00 / 3Z at 04:30, closed at 3.00 / 3Z, 60 samples; 05:00 peak 3.00 / 3Z at 05:00, closed at 3.00 / 3Z, 60 samples; 06:00 peak 1.33 / 1P at 06:40, closed at 1.33 / 1P, 60 samples; 07:00 peak 1.67 / 2M at 07:36, closed at 1.67 / 2M, 60 samples). 08:00 UTC bin is in progress (19 samples; peak 1.67 / 2M at 08:00; latest sample 1.33 / 1P at 08:18). estimated_kp remains below 5.0.

evidence.method: Read the public 1-minute estimated planetary K-index JSON. Use the latest published hour-start minute (08:00 UTC). Report last-180 and full published-window maxima.
evidence.limitations: estimated_kp is a near-real-time estimate, not the final observatory Kp. The public file is a rolling ~6-hour window (~358 samples), so earlier hours fall out of the file. The in-progress 08:00 UTC hour currently has 19 samples and may be revised as NOAA updates.

title.en: A magnitude 5.1 earthquake occurred 14 km WNW of Naze, Japan on 20 September 2026.
title.zh: 2026 年 9 月 20 日，日本名瀨西北西約 14 公里發生規模 5.1 地震。

summary.en: USGS M4.5+ day feed: mww 5.1, depth about 69 km. Newly listed this hour. Current day-feed maximum remains mb 5.3 (us7000tinl, Guam); tied in magnitude with mww 5.3 (us7000timy, Reykjanes Ridge).
summary.zh: USGS M4.5+ 一日饋送：mww 5.1，深度約 69 公里。本輪新上架。一日饋送目前最大仍為 mb 5.3（us7000tinl，關島）；規模同為 5.3 的還有 mww 5.3（us7000timy，雷克雅內斯海嶺）。

evidence.method: Added from the public USGS all-day M4.5+ GeoJSON feed when the event first appeared in the rolling 24-hour window.
evidence.limitations: Magnitudes and locations can be revised by USGS. The day feed only retains recent M4.5+ events.
